1978 United States Senate election in Illinois
The 1978 United States Senate election in Illinois took place on November 7, 1978; it was contested by incumbent Charles H. Percy and Democratic nominee Alex Seith.

Date on which the 1978 United States Senate election in Illinois took place.

Illinois
State where the 1978 United States Senate election took place.

United States Senate
Body to which Charles H. Percy ran for re-election to a third term in 1978.

Charles H. Percy
Incumbent Republican United States Senator who ran for re-election to a third term; he was opposed by Alex Seith and edged him out to win his third and final Senate term.

Alex Seith
Democratic nominee and attorney appointed to several local government positions; first-time candidate who opposed Charles H. Percy but was edged out.

William H. Cook Water Tank House

James P. Comer
Child psychiatrist born James Pierpont Comer on September 25, 1934 in East Chicago, Indiana. Currently the Maurice Falk Professor of Child Psychiatry at Yale Child Study Center since 1976 and an associate dean at Yale School of Medicine. Known for efforts to improve the scholastic performance of children from lower-income and minority backgrounds, which led to founding the Comer School Development Program in 1968. Author of ten books, more than 150 articles for Parents (magazine), and more than 300 articles on children's health and development and race relations.

Science Fantasy
British fantasy and science fiction magazine launched in 1950 by Nova Publications as a companion to New Worlds; it also appeared under the titles Impulse and SF Impulse, and ceased publication the following year after Roberts & Vinter came under financial pressure.

Impulse

New Worlds

John Carnell

Roberts & Vinter

Kyril Bonfiglioli

Androscoggin Bank Colisée
